title: The Rocket That Burns Thirteen Tonnes of Fuel Every Second
description: A comparison of the immense power generated by the Saturn V and the Space Launch System. These massive rockets represent the peak of human engineering and lunar exploration.
hook_card: The most powerful machines ever built

shots.narration: The Saturn V stood 110 metres tall and weighed about 2,900 tonnes when fully fuelled.
At liftoff, most of the mass is fuel, with the Apollo capsule making up a tiny fraction.
Its five F-1 engines burned roughly 13 tonnes of propellant every second during launch.
They produced about 34 million newtons of thrust, among the loudest sounds ever produced by a machine.
Thirteen Saturn Vs flew between 1967 and 1973, and every one of them succeeded.
NASA's Space Launch System stands 98 metres tall, flying its Artemis I mission in 2022.
At liftoff, the Space Launch System produces about 39 million newtons of thrust.
Rising into the sky, the modern rocket produces more thrust than the Saturn V.
